messages:
Alicia: Heads-up: saw 99th pct token latency spike in eu-west-1 dedicated pools this morning ~03:22 UTC. Pools A and B hit hard. Syslogs show repeated PCIe DMA timeouts on rack-3 hosts.
Ben: copying — dug into node-gpu-3-14 syslog, confirmed repeated DMA timeout and AER entries. snippet below.
Ben: ```Mar 10 03:22:13 gpu3 kernel: pcie_error: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) (Receiver ID) ... DMA timeout
Mar 10 03:22:14 gpu3 kernel: nvidia: Xid 61: GPU fault at ...```
Chandra: hmm could be noisy neighbor leading to host PCIe bandwidth saturation during KV cache flushes or big embedding batches. Any tenant spikes around 03:15-03:30?
Alicia: @Devon do you have tenant-level traces for pool A in that window?
Devon: pulling logs now. tenant-db had sustained heavy tensor uploads 03:18-03:25 (large batched embeddings). Also saw tenant-intelproj cron jobs co-scheduled on same hosts.
Chandra: proposal: immediate mitigations -> 1) soft-evict tenant-db to a burst-only/balanced pool, 2) move latency-sensitive tenants to pool-C soft-affinity, 3) enable `pcie_backoff=1` on affected nodes, 4) throttle host egress for sustained DMA patterns.
Ben: quick CLI to move: `redwood route update --tenant tenant-db --pool pool-c --strategy soft-affinity --canary 3%`
Alicia: I'll start a 3% canary and monitor 95/99 pct. infra-bot: schedule canary snapshot for metrics and traces.
infra-bot: canary snapshot scheduled: id=cs-1842001, targets=3% pool-c, start_ts=1842001400
Devon: migrated a few containers; immediate improvement in token latency on node-gpu-3-14. PCIe errors frequency reduced but not eliminated. Recommend host maintenance: NIC/BIOS firmware update and memtest overnight.
Chandra: agree. Also think we should add an egress QoS token-bucket for pool A to limit sustained host-to-host DMA bursts and prevent single tenants from saturating PCIe. I'll draft a short RFC with numbers.
Alicia: thanks — we should also add this incident to postmortems if root cause is noisy neighbor QoS. Filing incident note and tagging SRE. Keeping thread here for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
